questions.chapter_title: Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitution and Elimination Reactions
questions.question: What is the stereochemical outcome when (S)-2-bromobutane is treated with sodium cyanide in DMSO?

options.label: A
options.text: (S)-2-methylbutanenitrile with retention of configuration.

options.label: B
options.text: A 50:50 racemic mixture of (R) and (S).

options.label: C
options.text: (R)-2-methylbutanenitrile with 100% inversion of stereochemical configuration at the chiral center.

options.label: D
options.text: An optically inactive meso compound.

questions.correct_answer: (R)-2-methylbutanenitrile with 100% inversion of stereochemical configuration at the chiral center.
questions.explanation: Backside nucleophilic attack in an SN2 displacement forces complete stereochemical inversion (Walden inversion).

questions.chapter_title: Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitution and Elimination Reactions
questions.question: Why does solvolysis of (R)-3-bromo-3-methylhexane in water yield a mixture of (R)- and (S)-3-methyl-3-hexanol?

options.label: A
options.text: The reaction proceeds via an SN2 displacement.

options.label: B
options.text: Water inverts the stereochemistry twice.

options.label: C
options.text: Ionization generates a planar, achiral tertiary carbocation intermediate that is captured by water from both the top and bottom faces.

options.label: D
options.text: The product undergoes spontaneous ring closure.

questions.correct_answer: Ionization generates a planar, achiral tertiary carbocation intermediate that is captured by water from both the top and bottom faces.
questions.explanation: Planar sp² carbocations are achiral; attack from both faces produces a mixture of (R) and (S) enantiomers (racemization).

questions.chapter_title: Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitution and Elimination Reactions
questions.question: When (2R,3R)-2-bromo-3-phenylbutane is treated with NaOEt, which alkene stereoisomer is produced exclusively?

options.label: A
options.text: (E)-2-phenyl-2-butene.

options.label: B
options.text: 2-phenyl-1-butene.

options.label: C
options.text: 3-phenyl-1-butene.

options.label: D
options.text: (Z)-2-phenyl-2-butene, dictated by the strict anti-periplanar alignment of the β-hydrogen and leaving group bromine.

questions.correct_answer: (Z)-2-phenyl-2-butene, dictated by the strict anti-periplanar alignment of the β-hydrogen and leaving group bromine.
questions.explanation: Conformational rotation to achieve anti-periplanar alignment places the phenyl and methyl groups in the (Z) orientation upon elimination.

questions.chapter_title: Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitution and Elimination Reactions
questions.topic: Menthyl vs Neomenthyl Chloride E2 Elimination Rates
questions.question: Why does neomenthyl chloride eliminate 200 times faster than menthyl chloride with NaOEt?

options.label: A
options.text: In neomenthyl chloride, the chlorine atom is already axial in the most stable chair conformer, ready for anti-periplanar E2 elimination with adjacent hydrogens.

options.label: B
options.text: Neomenthyl chloride is an aromatic molecule.

options.label: C
options.text: Neomenthyl chloride reacts via an SN1 mechanism.

options.label: D
options.text: Menthyl chloride contains no chlorine atoms.

questions.correct_answer: In neomenthyl chloride, the chlorine atom is already axial in the most stable chair conformer, ready for anti-periplanar E2 elimination with adjacent hydrogens.
questions.explanation: Neomenthyl chloride has an axial chlorine in its major diequatorial conformer, avoiding the energetic penalty of flipping to an unstable chair.

questions.chapter_title: Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitution and Elimination Reactions
questions.question: What stereochemical configuration is obtained when (2R,3R)-3-bromobutan-2-ol is treated with aqueous NaOH?

options.label: A
options.text: cis-2,3-dimethyloxirane.

options.label: B
options.text: meso-2,3-butanediol.

options.label: C
options.text: trans-2,3-dimethyloxirane (inversion at C3 upon intramolecular backside attack by the deprotonated alkoxide oxygen).

options.label: D
options.text: 2-butanone.

questions.correct_answer: trans-2,3-dimethyloxirane (inversion at C3 upon intramolecular backside attack by the deprotonated alkoxide oxygen).
questions.explanation: Deprotonation creates an alkoxide that attacks the adjacent C-Br carbon from the backside, inverting C3 to produce the trans-epoxide.

questions.chapter_title: Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitution and Elimination Reactions
questions.topic: Retention of Configuration via Neighboring Group Participation
questions.question: Why does treatment of (2S,3R)-3-(methylthio)butan-2-ol with TsCl followed by acetate yield an acetate product with net retention of configuration?

options.label: A
options.text: Sulfur oxidizes the carbon atom.

options.label: B
options.text: The sulfur atom attacks intramolecularly to form a cyclic sulfonium ion with inversion, followed by a second intermolecular attack by acetate with inversion (double inversion = net retention).

options.label: C
options.text: The molecule is an achiral meso compound.

options.label: D
options.text: The reaction proceeds through a radical intermediate.

questions.correct_answer: The sulfur atom attacks intramolecularly to form a cyclic sulfonium ion with inversion, followed by a second intermolecular attack by acetate with inversion (double inversion = net retention).
questions.explanation: Two consecutive SN2 backside displacements (anchimeric assistance) result in net overall retention of absolute stereochemistry.

questions.chapter_title: Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitution and Elimination Reactions
questions.question: Why must halohydrins adopt an anti-periplanar conformation between the alkoxide oxygen and halogen for epoxide closure?

options.label: A
options.text: Halohydrins are planar molecules.

options.label: B
options.text: The alkoxide must attack the halogen atom directly.

options.label: C
options.text: The alkoxide lone pair must align at 180° directly opposite the C-X σ* antibonding orbital to execute the intramolecular SN2 displacement.

options.label: D
options.text: A syn conformation is required to form a four-membered ring.

questions.correct_answer: The alkoxide lone pair must align at 180° directly opposite the C-X σ* antibonding orbital to execute the intramolecular SN2 displacement.
questions.explanation: Intramolecular SN2 requires strict collinear alignment of the nucleophilic oxygen lone pair and the C-X σ* antibonding orbital.

questions.chapter_title: Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitution and Elimination Reactions
questions.topic: Chiral Alkyl Halide SN2 Reaction with Inversion Verification
questions.question: What is the absolute configuration of the product when (R)-2-chloropentane is treated with sodium ethanethiolate (NaSEt)?

options.label: A
options.text: (±)-2-(ethylthio)pentane (racemic).

options.label: B
options.text: 1-(ethylthio)pentane.

options.label: C
options.text: (R)-2-(ethylthio)pentane.

options.label: D
options.text: (S)-2-(ethylthio)pentane, resulting from clean SN2 inversion of the (R) stereocenter.

questions.correct_answer: (S)-2-(ethylthio)pentane, resulting from clean SN2 inversion of the (R) stereocenter.
questions.explanation: Direct backside displacement of chloride by ethanethiolate inverts the chiral center from (R) to (S).

questions.chapter_title: Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitution and Elimination Reactions
questions.topic: Stereospecific Elimination of Meso vs d,l Substrates
questions.question: What alkene stereoisomer is formed from the E2 elimination of meso-1,2-dibromo-1,2-diphenylethane with base?

options.label: A
options.text: Diphenylacetylene directly.

options.label: B
options.text: A 50:50 mixture of (E) and (Z).

options.label: C
options.text: (E)-1-bromo-1,2-diphenylethane exclusively.

options.label: D
options.text: (Z)-1-bromo-1,2-diphenylethane exclusively.

questions.correct_answer: (E)-1-bromo-1,2-diphenylethane exclusively.
questions.explanation: Anti-periplanar alignment of H and Br in the meso diastereomer forces the two bulky phenyl rings into opposite (E) geometry upon elimination.

options.label: C
